name: Genome Nexus
description: Genome Nexus is a resource designed for the rapid and automated annotation and interpretation of genetic variants associated with cancer. It consolidates data from various existing databases to provide comprehensive insights into genetic mutations, including their conversion from DNA to protein changes, functional effects of protein mutations, mutation frequencies, gene functions, variant effects, and clinical actionability. This integration aims to facilitate high-throughput analysis, making it easier for researchers and clinicians to understand the implications of genetic variants in cancer.
rawDescription:
# Genome Nexus 🧬

Genome Nexus, a comprehensive one-stop resource for fast, automated and
high-throughput annotation and interpretation of genetic variants in cancer.
Genome Nexus integrates information from a variety of existing resources,
including databases that convert DNA changes to protein changes, predict the
functional effects of protein mutations, and contain information about mutation
frequencies, gene function, variant effects, and clinical actionability.

## Documentation 📖
See the [docs](https://docs.genomenexus.org)

## Run 💻

### Alternative 1 - run genome-nexus, mongoDB and genome-nexus-vep in docker containers
First, set environment variables for Ensembl Release, VEP Assembly, location of VEP Cache, and species (since a mouse instalation is supported). If these are not, the default values from `.env` will be set.

The reference genome and Ensembl release must be consistent with a version in [genome-nexus-importer/data/](https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-importer/tree/master/data).
For example `grch37_ensembl92`, `grch38_ensembl92` or `grch38_ensembl95`:
```
export REF_ENSEMBL_VERSION=grch38_ensembl92
```
If you want to setup Genome Nexus for mouse, also set the `SPECIES` variable to 'mus_musculus'. Also see the [docs](https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-importer/blob/master/docs/setup-genome-nexus-mouse.md) to create a mouse database.
```bash
export SPECIES=mus_musculus
```

If you would like to do local VEP annotations instead of using the public Ensembl API, please uncomment `# gn_vep.region.url=http://localhost:6060/vep/human/region/VARIANT` in your `application.properties`. This will require you to download the VEP cache files for the preferred Ensembl Release and Reference genome, see our documentation on [downloading the Genome Nexus VEP Cache](https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-vep/blob/master/README.md#create-vep-cache). This will take several hours.
```
# Set local cache dir
export VEP_CACHE=<local_vep_cache>

# GRCh38 or GRCh37
export VEP_ASSEMBLY=GRCh38
```

Run docker-compose to create images and containers:
```
docker-compose up --build -d
```

Run without recreating images:
```
docker-compose up -d
```

Run without Genome Nexus VEP:
```
# Start both the Web and DB (dependency of Web) containers
docker-compose up -d web
```

Stop and remove containers:
```
docker-compose down
```

### Alternative 2 - run genome-nexus locally, but mongoDB in docker container
```
# the genomenexus/gn-mongo images comes with all the required tables imported
# change latest to different version if necessary (only need to run this once)
docker run --name=gn-mongo --restart=always -p 27017:27017 -d genomenexus/gn-mongo:latest 
mvn  -DskipTests clean install
java -jar web/target/web-*.war
```

### Alternative 3 - install mongoDB locally and run with local java
Install mongoDB manually. Then follow instructions in
[genome-nexus-importer](https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-importer)
to initialize the database.

After that run this:
```
mvn clean install
java -jar web/target/web-*.war
```

highLevelGoals: Enable researchers to conduct thorough studies on genetic variants by providing integrated and detailed information about mutations and their implications in cancer.
Support clinicians in making informed decisions regarding patient treatment by providing clear interpretations of genetic data and its clinical relevance.
Allow data analysts to efficiently analyze and derive insights from consolidated genetic data, improving the speed and accuracy of their analyses.
lowLevelGoals: Allow researchers to fetch detailed information about specific genetic variants from the database.
Enable researchers to submit a request for analysis of selected genetic variants to receive insights and implications.
Allow clinicians to retrieve clinical interpretations and recommendations based on genetic data for patient treatment.
Enable clinicians to input and log patient-specific genetic data into the system for analysis and interpretation.
Allow data analysts to combine multiple genetic datasets into a single view for easier analysis.
Enable data analysts to run algorithms on consolidated genetic data to extract meaningful insights and trends.
Allow researchers to request a comparison between different genetic variants to understand their differences and similarities.
Enable clinicians to update existing patient genetic data in the system for accurate analysis and interpretation.
Allow data analysts to export consolidated genetic data for external analysis or reporting purposes.
Allow researchers to retrieve metadata associated with genetic variants, such as frequency and population data.
Enable clinicians to log clinical recommendations based on genetic interpretations for future reference.
Allow data analysts to analyze trends in genetic data over time to identify patterns and anomalies.

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are well-aligned with the software description and the defined actors. They correctly capture the core functional purpose of Genome Nexus
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: Major omission. The software description explicitly states that Genome Nexus provides "conversion from DNA to protein changes" and "functional effects of protein mutations." The provided low-level goals focus on retrieving data, submitting requests, and analyzing trends, but they completely omit the specific functional capability of converting DNA variants to protein changes or retrieving functional effect annotations. These are core features described in the system's purpose. Additionally, the description mentions "clinical actionability," which is only vaguely covered by "Access Clinical Interpretation," but the specific action of retrieving actionability status is missing. The low-level goals are too generic and miss the specific domain functionalities (DNA-to-protein conversion, functional effects) highlighted in the description.
